questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, Nature first draws a type profile $\theta$ from $p$. What does player $i$ know when she chooses her action?
options: Every player's realised type, since types are drawn publicly
Her own realised type $\theta_i$, but not the others' types
No realised type at all, not even her own
The others' actions, which are chosen before hers

questions.question: In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$, suppose every type set $\Theta_i$ contains a single type. What kind of game is it then?
options: Still a game of incomplete information, since $p$ is used
A game with no pure strategies, since types are missing
An ordinary normal-form game of complete information
An extensive-form game in which Nature moves last

questions.question: In a Bayesian game, player 2's type is $x$ with probability $0.4$ and $y$ with probability $0.6$, independent of player 1's type. Player 2 plays $L$ if $x$ and $R$ if $y$. Player 1's action $U$ pays 5 against $L$ and 1 against $R$. What is $U$'s interim expected payoff?

In a Bayesian game, two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth 1 to each is provided iff at least one contributes, and a contributor $i$ pays her cost type $\theta_i$. Player 2 contributes whatever her type. Comparing interim expected payoffs, which action is better for player 1 of type $\theta_1=\tfrac{1}{4}$?
In a two-player Bayesian game, player 1 has 2 actions and 3 types; player 2 has 3 actions and 2 types. How many pure strategy profiles $(s_1,s_2)$ are there?
In a Bayesian game $\langle N,\{A_i\},\{\Theta_i\},\{v_i\},p\rangle$ with two players, player 1 has two possible types while player 2 has a single type. Which description of the game is correct?
options: It is a normal-form game of complete information, since player 2 has no private information
It is not a game at all, since the players have unequal information
It is a Bayesian game in which player 2 faces uncertainty about player 1's type
It is a Bayesian game in which player 1 is uncertain about her own type

questions.question: In a Bayesian game, types have prior $p(a,x)=0.4$, $p(a,y)=0.1$, $p(b,x)=0.2$, $p(b,y)=0.3$ ($\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$, $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$). Player 1's action Invest pays 6 if $\theta_2=x$ and $-3$ if $\theta_2=y$. What is its interim expected payoff for type $b$?

In a Bayesian game, two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth 1 to each is provided iff at least one contributes, and a contributor $i$ pays her cost type $\theta_i$. Types $\theta_i\in\{\tfrac{1}{4},2\}$ are independent with $P(\tfrac{1}{4})=0.3$. Each player contributes iff her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$. What is player 1's ex ante expected payoff, averaging over both players' types?
